Consult Summary:
- 51-year-old female with 6 days of dysuria, malodorous urine, intermittent midline lower abdominal pain and visible blood spots in urine; clinician suspects lower urinary tract infection and prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics (antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented).

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Pain when urinating (dysuria), unpleasant/foul smell to urine, and spotting of blood in urine for 6 days.
  - Intermittent lower abdominal (suprapubic/midline) pain, severity 7/10, comes and goes.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms started 6 days ago and have persisted; patient reports no prior similar episodes.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific initiating activity identified (no recent increased exercise, dehydration, or increased sexual activity according to patient).
  - Advised to drink increased fluids; no current other relieving measures documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Denies fever or feeling feverish.
  - Denies loin/back pain (transcript includes an unclear statement regarding lower back pain; see Quality checks).
  - Denies vaginal discharge.
  - No change in bowel habit, weight loss, or blood in stool.
  - Able to eat and drink normally.
- Menstrual history:
  - Regular periods.
- Other relevant negatives:
  - No prior urinary tract infections reported.
  - No recent surgeries reported.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) — patient reports history; no recent change reported.
- No other chronic medical problems documented.

Medications:
- Mebeverine 200 mg, three times daily (patient-reported; dose/frequency confirmed in transcript).
- Antibiotic prescribed for presumed UTI — name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.

Allergies:
- Clindamycin.

Social History:
- Lives with friends.
- Occupation: support worker.
- Alcohol: occasional; approximately one glass of wine per week.
- Tobacco: denies smoking.
- No other substance use reported.
- No financial or other lifestyle concerns documented.

Family History:
- No family medical problems reported.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- Vitals: not recorded.

Investigations:
- No urine dip, urine culture, blood tests, or imaging performed or reported.
- Clinician recommended patient obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature.
- Clinician noted that usually treatment can proceed without urine testing for a typical lower UTI.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute lower urinary tract infection (uncomplicated cystitis)
  - Assessment: Dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and hematuria (spots) consistent with lower UTI; no fever reported.
  - Plan:
    - Prescribe a 3-day course of antibiotics — prescription to be sent to the patient’s requested pharmacy (Knightsbridge Practice). (Antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented.)
    - Start antibiotics as soon as obtained; expect medication to be available at pharmacy in ~1 hour (clinician advised to allow at least one hour).
    - Advise increased oral fluids (recommendation stated: 2.5–3.0 liters per day).
    - Consider cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary acidity/alkalinizing sachets (patient advised these “may help”).
    - Obtain and monitor temperature at home; if temperature rises or patient feels feverish, seek review.
    - Return or re-contact if symptoms worsen, if lower back/loin pain develops, if difficulty passing urine occurs, or if symptoms do not resolve after treatment or recur.
- Issue 2: Hematuria (macroscopic/microscopic blood spots in urine with current episode)
  - Assessment: Hematuria reported as part of current urinary symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor response to antibiotic treatment.
    - Re-evaluate if hematuria persists or recurs (further investigation would be required if not resolving; specific tests not documented).
- Issue 3: Irritable bowel syndrome (stable)
  - Assessment: History of IBS; no active bowel symptoms or change reported.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily as patient is taking.
    - No additional GI management documented.

- General plan items:
  - No routine follow-up required if symptoms resolve after treatment.
  - Patient instructed to seek prompt review if symptoms worsen, fever develops, flank/loin pain appears, or urinary retention occurs.
  - Prescription to be sent to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy (patient to collect and start medication).

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No physical examination documented (abdominal, external genital, or pelvic exam) — expected in many in-person assessments.
  - No recorded vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure).
  - No urine dipstick, urinalysis, or urine culture results documented.
  - Antibiotic name, dose, route, and frequency not documented.
  - No pregnancy status or pregnancy test documented (relevant for antibiotic selection in women of childbearing age).
  - No STI screening history or sexual history documented.
  - No explicit plan for follow-up testing if hematuria persists (patient advised to re-contact but specific investigations not listed).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Ambiguous statements regarding lower back/loin pain: patient at times provided unclear responses when asked about lower back pain; later specifically denied loin pain. (Conflict noted.)
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall conversation reasonably clear; occasional brief repetitions and one unclear exchange about lower back pain. No major portions unintelligible.
